clips.text_zh: 睇到呢張圖真係喊出嚟。15年前死慳死慳擺1K美金入BTC，依家值8.97M。我就係遲咗入場嗰個。算啦，又係學費。btw 我嗰個prop firm account又輸多2K，lol。
clips.text_en_b1: $1,000 invested 15 years ago today would be worth: Bitcoin $8,970,000, Nvidia $735,000, Tesla $231,000, Apple $29,000, S&P $8,400, Gold $2,150. Posted on /biz/ today with the usual cope about early movers winning everything.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread comparing 15-year returns of major assets

signal.rationale: OP framing implies BTC is the only asset that meaningfully outperformed, implicit long bias

clips.text_en_b2: $1,000 invested fifteen years ago today would have ballooned into: Bitcoin $8,970,000, Nvidia $735,000, Tesla $231,000, Apple $29,000, S&P $8,400, and Gold $2,150. OP on /biz/ posted the chart and is clearly devastated, mourning the fact that he missed the boat entirely. He copes by adding that his prop firm account just bled another 2K, so at least his losses remain somewhat consistent across the board.
clips.text_en_c1: A chart circulating on /biz/ today has prompted the usual hand-wringing from those who arrived late to the party. Had one allocated a mere thousand dollars fifteen years ago, that position in Bitcoin would now be valued at approximately 8.97 million dollars, dwarfing even Nvidia at 735K, Tesla at 231K, Apple at 29K, the S&P at 8.4K, and gold at a paltry 2.15K. The poster laments being a late entrant, attributing the missed fortune to tuition paid in hindsight rather than foresight.
clips.text_en_c2: Encountering that chart on /biz/ today provoked the customary lament among anons who arrived late to the trade: a thousand dollars allocated fifteen years ago would, by present valuations, have compounded into roughly 8.97 million in Bitcoin, dwarfing Nvidia's 735,000, Tesla's 231,000, Apple's comparatively pedestrian 29,000, the S&P's 8,400, and even gold, which limped to a mere 2,150 over the identical horizon. The familiar cope ensued, with veterans congratulating themselves for having possessed the conviction to enter when entry still felt preposterous. The poster himself, ruefully, was not among them. Tallying his own miscues, he noted that his proprietary trading account had hemorrhaged an additional two thousand dollars in recent sessions, a footnote that rather vividly encapsulated the bittersweet arithmetic of asymmetric regret, lessons paid for in full and remembered far longer than any gains.

clips.text_zh: Robotaxi個network真係concept幾work。如果可以用prop firm嘅錢買幾架Cybercab擺落去收租，passive income咪解決晒我嘅cash flow問題。可惜個drawdown仲未止血，考牌都未搞掂，諗都多餘。
clips.text_en_b1: Redpill me on buying Cybercabs and putting them to work on the Tesla Robotaxi network for passive income. OP is asking /biz/ whether owning the cars directly and listing them on the network beats just holding TSLA shares through the same upside.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking if buying Cybercabs directly beats holding TSLA

signal.rationale: OP is exploring direct exposure to Tesla's robotaxi thesis, implicit long TSLA bias

clips.text_en_b2: Convince me on purchasing Cybercabs outright and deploying them across the Tesla Robotaxi network to generate passive income. OP on /biz/ wants to know whether actually owning the vehicles and listing them on the network yields better returns than simply holding TSLA shares through the same upside. The premise sounds solid in theory, though his drawdown has not stopped bleeding and he has not even passed the licensing exam yet.
clips.text_en_c1: A /biz/ thread poses a genuinely intriguing proposition regarding the Tesla Robotaxi network and its potential for generating genuine passive income streams. The original poster contemplates deploying capital, ideally borrowed through a prop firm arrangement, to acquire several Cybercabs outright and register them on the network as revenue-generating assets. The implicit argument is that direct ownership of the vehicles, earning a share of fares per ride, could outperform simply holding TSLA equity with its correlated but diluted exposure to robotaxi upside.
clips.text_en_c2: An enterprising anon solicited the board's collective wisdom regarding a rather elegant proposition: whether one might procure a fleet of Tesla's forthcoming Cybercabs, deploy them onto the nascent Robotaxi network, and thereby convert depreciating hardware into a comparatively dependable stream of passive income, ostensibly superior to the passive appreciation afforded by merely holding TSLA equity through the same secular tailwind. The premise, he conceded, was conceptually sound, the operational math favorable, and the diversification rationale impeccable. Reality, alas, intervened with its customary indignities. His proprietary trading account remained mired in an obstinate drawdown that had yet to show any inclination toward mean reversion, and the licensing prerequisites for actually executing the strategy remained conspicuously unaddressed. Speculation, in other words, had outpaced implementation by a considerable margin.

clips.text_zh: OpenAI出GPT-6 Astra喇。話自己係最強、最align嘅model，benchmark直接saturate晒。作為一個surveyor我而家仲有工打，遲啲連AP都唔使我簽，AI直接畫晒圖。廢柴如我，真係靠AI續命。
clips.text_en_b1: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra and says welcome to the AGI era. The company describes it as the world's most intelligent and aligned model, and the benchmarks seem to back that up. It nearly saturates ARC-AGI 3 and the OGRE eval, beating every prior model on coding and reasoning tasks.

signal.rationale: AI capability update, no direct trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: OpenAI has rolled out GPT-6 Astra and is essentially declaring the AGI era officially underway. The company bills it as the most intelligent and aligned model on the planet, and the benchmarks appear to confirm the hype, with ARC-AGI 3 and the OGRE eval nearly maxed out. A surveyor posted on /g/ wondering how long his job will last before the AI simply handles everything end to end.
clips.text_en_c1: OpenAI has officially unveiled GPT-6 Astra, heralding what the company confidently describes as the dawn of the AGI era. The model is being marketed as the most intellectually capable and rigorously aligned system ever released, a claim that the benchmark results would appear to substantiate. Astra reportedly approaches saturation on ARC-AGI 3 and the OGRE evaluation, decisively outpacing every predecessor on coding and complex reasoning tasks. A working surveyor posting on /g/ notes the irony that his profession may have a finite shelf life, since AI systems are increasingly capable of producing the technical drawings that currently require an licensed architect's signature.
clips.text_en_c2: OpenAI, in a release that landed with the subtlety of a thunderclap, unveiled GPT-6 Astra and cordially invited observers to welcome the long-anticipated arrival of artificial general intelligence. The model, according to the company's own framing, constitutes the most capable and most rigorously aligned system yet deployed, a claim that the published benchmarks appeared to validate with almost unseemly thoroughness; Astra reportedly approaches saturation on ARC-AGI 3 and the OGRE evaluation, while decisively outscoring every predecessor on tasks demanding sustained reasoning, programmatic synthesis, and structured problem decomposition. For one anonymous surveyor currently employed in a profession that interprets precisely such outputs, the implications carried a distinctly personal valence. He wondered aloud whether, within a matter of months, even the rubric of an accredited professional might prove superfluous to the workflow.

clips.text_zh: 有個anon去咗芬蘭，由Helsinki機場一路去到Rovaniemi都見到同樣情況。仲有印度人同其他亞洲mix。睇完好有feel，HK都係咁，越嚟越逼。我想去US唔係冇原因嘅，廢物都想要返啲space。
clips.text_en_b1: Anon lands in Helsinki airport and sees the demographic shift immediately. Takes the train to Tampere, then Oulu, then Rovaniemi and it is the same story everywhere. Says it is the tip of the iceberg and notes Indians and mixed Asian groups alongside the African migrants across Finnish cities.
clips.text_en_b2: An anon lands at Helsinki airport and the demographic shift hits him straight away. He takes the train up to Tampere, then pushes on to Oulu and finally Rovaniemi, only to find the same picture playing out in every city. He frames it as the tip of the iceberg and points out Indians alongside mixed Asian groups joining the African migrants scattered across Finland, which prompted a broader rant about overcrowding.
clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous poster on /pol/ recounts a journey that began at Helsinki airport and culminated in Rovaniemi, with stops in Tampere and Oulu along the way. His observation is strikingly consistent: the demographic transformation is unmistakable from the moment one clears customs. He notes substantial South Asian populations alongside the more frequently discussed African migrants, suggesting that whatever narrative prevails in domestic discourse captures only the tip of a far larger iceberg. The poster draws an explicit parallel with Hong Kong, which he characterises as increasingly congested and spatially suffocating.
clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous correspondent, having alighted at Helsinki-Vantaa, chronicled a demographic transformation that evidently commenced upon arrival and proved entirely undiminished across hundreds of kilometers of subsequent rail travel. From the capital southward to Tampere, onward through Oulu, and ultimately to the sub-Arctic terminus of Rovaniemi, the composition of public space remained remarkably consistent: substantial contingents of African migrants, supplemented by Indian arrivals and an assortment of mixed Asian groupings whose presence the poster found conspicuously difficult to dismiss as incidental. He characterized the visible pattern as merely the visible apex of a far more considerable submerged mass. The observation provoked in him an acute sense of spatial compression, a phenomenon he insisted was hardly confined to Nordic latitudes; Hong Kong, he noted curtly, exhibited rather analogous tendencies.

clips.text_zh: 有隻eroge喺日本Steam排第一，仲高過晒啲AAA PC大作。LOL都俾人打下個台啦。日本仔打機口味真係好難理解，S15都睇緊T1 vs GenG，呢邊啲人就去買eroge，lol。
clips.text_en_b1: An eroge is currently ranked number one on Steam in Japan, outselling every major AAA PC release in the region. OP cannot believe an adult visual novel beat out all the big budget Western and Japanese PC launches this week on the Japanese store chart.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread shocked an eroge is #1 on Japan Steam
clips.text_en_b2: An eroge has somehow climbed to the number one spot on Steam in Japan, outselling every major AAA PC release currently available. OP on /v/ is in disbelief that an adult visual novel managed to outpace all the big budget Western and Japanese PC launches this week on the Japanese store chart. Meanwhile competitive gaming fans were busy watching T1 versus GenG, so priorities clearly differ across the island.
clips.text_en_c1: In what can only be described as a watershed moment for the Japanese PC gaming market, an eroge has claimed the coveted number one position on Steam's regional charts, decisively outselling every major AAA release available on the platform this week. The /v/ thread captures a genuine sense of bewilderment, as both Western blockbusters and flagship Japanese PC titles have been comprehensively humbled by what is, at its core, an adult visual novel. The poster finds the Japanese gaming palate altogether inscrutable, juxtaposing this phenomenon with the parallel reality that domestic esports audiences remain fixated on fixtures such as the T1 versus GenG series, while their compatriots are busy purchasing,…
clips.text_en_c2: An adult visual novel currently occupies the apex position on Steam's Japanese storefront, comprehensively outselling every marquee PC release that Western and domestic publishers had presumed would dominate the weekly rankings. The original poster, a self-described connoisseur of conventional gaming hierarchies, professed himself genuinely staggered that a category routinely dismissed as niche could eclipse high-budget productions engineered through hundreds of millions of dollars of development expenditure. The juxtaposition invited broader commentary on the seeming incomprehensibility of Japanese consumer preferences, a sensibility further underlined by the simultaneous cultural fact of T1 versus GenG drawing massive concurrent viewership in Seoul, while a parallel demographic in Osaka and Tokyo, by apparent consensus, elected to purchase illustrated eroge instead.

clips.text_zh: 呢條友OHP就嚟上1pl8，bench連2pl8都未到。睇完我更加覺得自己係廢物。肥仔信今日又tag我話一齊gym，我都唔知應唔應該應機，考牌溫書都未開。
clips.text_en_b1: OP is closer to a 1-plate overhead press than he is to a 2-plate bench, 3-plate squat, or 4-plate deadlift. He expects to hit a clean 1-plate OHP for reps within a month or two while the other three lifts still lag behind his bodyweight.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about lift ratios and OHP progress
clips.text_en_b2: OP is tantalisingly close to a one-plate overhead press while his bench still cannot crack two plates, his squat lags behind three, and his deadlift is nowhere near four plates. He reckons he will nail a clean OHP for reps within a month or two, yet the other three lifts stubbornly refuse to keep pace with his bodyweight. Classic case of one lift carrying the entire physique.
clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ regular has posted a strength profile that defies conventional expectations in ways that would be comedic if it were not so painfully relatable. His overhead press is tantalisingly close to a one-plate milestone, a feat he expects to achieve for clean reps within the next month or two, while his bench press languishes below the two-plate mark. His squat remains anchored below three plates and his deadlift has yet to breach the four-plate threshold, with each lift conspicuously trailing his bodyweight.
clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous regular of /fit/ confessed, with the particular candor endemic to strength-training forums, that his overhead press had crept within striking distance of a single forty-kilogram plate while his bench press had yet to clear ninety kilograms, his squat remained stubbornly beneath one hundred and forty, and his deadlift had failed to crest one hundred and eighty. The configuration, statistically improbable and aesthetically ungainly, led him to anticipate a clean single-plate press for repetitions within a matter of weeks, even as the remaining three compound movements continued to languish conspicuously beneath his bodyweight. His fat friend, perpetual in unsolicited encouragement, had once again extended an invitation to train together, an offer the poster found himself disinclined to accept while licensure examinations loomed and revision materials remained, in his own telling, distressingly untouched.

clips.text_zh: 鬼滅俾人鬧咗咁多年，我啱啱先睇到season 2。其實d criticism擺喺其他作品度一樣work，只係佢賺咗幾十億先被針對。考牌溫到攰就煲返兩集，動畫真係靠佢續命。
clips.text_en_b1: Watching Demon Slayer for the first time, currently on season 2. OP asks why so many people trash the series when every criticism leveled at it applies equally to other beloved anime. Says the only real difference is Demon Slayer made billions of dollars at the box office.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread defending Demon Slayer against haters
clips.text_en_b2: Just started Demon Slayer for the first time and I am currently working through season 2. OP on /a/ argues that every criticism levelled at the series applies just as easily to plenty of other beloved anime, so the real reason it gets trashed is simply that it raked in billions at the box office. Success breeds resentment, essentially, and the show did nothing wrong besides print money.
clips.text_en_c1: Having finally committed to watching Demon Slayer and progressing through season two, a /a/ poster has articulated a defence of the franchise that resonates with anyone fatigued by the seemingly endless cycle of online criticism. He argues with considerable rhetorical force that the standard objections levelled against the series, ranging from derivative plotting to shallow character development, apply with equal validity to countless other anime that enjoy uncritical adoration from the same vocal communities. The only substantive distinction, in his estimation, is commercial: Demon Slayer has generated billions at the box office, and apparently massive financial success is itself sufficient grounds for sustained hostility.
clips.text_en_c2: Having only recently commenced Demon Slayer and finding himself midway through the second season, an anonymous contributor to /a/ posed a question that has animated arguments across the medium for years: why, precisely, does the franchise attract such disproportionate opprobrium when the criticisms routinely marshalled against its plotting, its sentimentality, and its conspicuous reliance on formula apply with equal vigor to a great many celebrated works now enshrined in the canon? His tentative conclusion, delivered without excessive solemnity, was that animus correlates rather neatly with commercial magnitude: Demon Slayer earned billions at the box office, and billions, he observed, tend to attract a rather specific species of retroactive aesthetic objection.
